facts.claim: F5V main-sequence primary delivers peak irradiance at ~480 nm with bolometric luminosity 1.35 L☉.
facts.justification: F-type stellar SEDs peak in the blue with elevated high-energy photon output compared to G-types; UV excess is driven by spectral type and thin O₃ column, not heliocentric distance.

facts.claim: M3V red dwarf companion provides steady thermal baseline with frequent optical/UV flare spikes.
facts.justification: M-dwarfs dominate the infrared spectrum; flare activity is common but primarily emits UV/X-ray/optical, not IR pulses. The companion supplies a persistent ~900 nm NIR photon bias that heats surface targets.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

Flare spikes increase mutagenic dose and atmospheric ionization.

facts.claim: Circumbinary (P-type) orbit at 1.15 AU with a 387-day period.
facts.justification: Kepler’s third law scaled to combined binary mass (~1.35 M☉); dynamically stable only if binary separation is <0.2 AU and eccentricity is low.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)
